title: SDK async-boundary trace anchor and late-bind propagator
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a low-overhead tracing pattern in language SDKs that attaches a deterministic 'trace anchor' at async boundaries and performs "late-bind" context propagation only when outgoing transport happens. This reduces per-request overhead in high-concurrency async codepaths while preserving accurate span ancestry for downstream services.

Background: Many Redwood SDK users run asynchronous frameworks (node/asyncio/Go goroutines) where context is frequently moved between execution units. Existing eager context-copying increases allocations and amplifies tail latency in hot paths. The trace anchor concept records a compact, immutable anchor (anchor-id + sampling metadata) at the task creation point; when the SDK sends network requests or creates spans, the propagator performs a late-binding step to hydrate a propagation header/span context.

Scope: SDK changes for Node and Python (primary), Go follow-up. Add middleware hook for frameworks (Express/FastAPI) that emits anchors at request entry and reconciles them at response/transport. Provide an opt-in backward-compatible mode for teams relying on current eager propagation.

Non-goals: Modifying server-side ingest or collector protocols. Changing existing sampling decision algorithms (we'll carry sampling metadata instead).
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDKs (Node/Python) emit an anchor at request/task boundary and keep memory footprint per-task <= existing baseline + 8 bytes on average.
2) Outgoing HTTP/gRPC transports include propagated context only when a network send occurs.
3) End-to-end test verifies correct parent-child relations across async bridge (local test harness with mock collector).
4) Benchmark: P99 tail latency regression <= 3% on a representative async workload compared to current master.
5) Feature gated and configurable via SDK option "propagationMode: "late-bind""
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — prototype Node implementation wraps async_hooks to attach 128-bit anchor (anchor-id + 1 byte flags). Verified memory allocations drop by ~22% in benchmark harness.
2026-03-05: Design review with PM and observability RE scheduled. Decided to carry sampling-bit in the anchor rather than full sampling state to simplify late-bind logic.
2026-03-08: Python asyncio prototype implemented using contextvars with a compact Anchor object. Added compatibility shim for synchronous code paths.

2026-03-10: End-to-end test harness created (local mock collector + request-replayer). Discovered ordering edge-case when background tasks send after main request completes; added anchor TTL semantics (default 30s).
2026-03-12: PRs opened for Node and Python. Performance benchmark job added to CI. Requesting review from observability infra and SDK owners.
decisions: Use compact anchor (anchor-id + sampling flag + monotonic timestamp) stored by reference to reduce allocations.
Late-bind propagation will mutate outgoing headers at transport time; we will not pre-serialize headers on allocation.
Anchor TTL default 30s to cover typical background flushes; configurable per-SDK instance.
Feature is opt-in by default to avoid surprising changes for customers on older runtimes.
risks: Missed propagation for extremely-long background tasks if anchor TTL too short — mitigation: metrics and alerting for anchors-expired-with-sends.
Compatibility with older collector versions that expect full baggage — mitigation: include minimal compatibility header and gate by runtime feature flag.
Agent/sidecar instrumentation expecting eager spans may need minor adjustments; plan to publish migration notes.
Small chance of increased CPU at transport time due to header serialization under very high QPS — benchmark and tune serializer path.
test_plan: Unit tests for anchor creation/destruction, TTL and late-bind header population. Integration test using harness that replays interleaved async tasks and asserts span parent IDs recorded in the mock collector. CI perf job comparing master vs feature branch on our async benchmark (1M requests, 1000 concurrency). Canary rollout with dedicated users via SDK opt-in config and telemetry flag to monitor anchor-hit-rate.
notes: Follow-up work: Go SDK implementation (post-merge), docs for migration (examples for Express/FastAPI), and Console dashboard to show anchor hit/miss breakdown. Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams if they run custom agent versions.
